title: PB Fintech Profit Jumps 92% as Policybazaar's Insurance Engine Fires on All Cylinders
excerpt: The Policybazaar parent reported operating revenues of Rs 1,888 crore for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA expanding fourfold as margin gains accelerated across the insurance platform.
body:
• PB Fintech's net profit surged 92% year-on-year to Rs 163 crore in Q1 FY27, with EBITDA expanding fourfold to Rs 139 crore
  • Operating revenues rose 40% to Rs 1,888 crore, driven by a 41% jump in total insurance premiums to Rs 8,372 crore
  • Profit margins improved to 9% from 6% a year ago, with the core online insurance business generating Rs 1,194 crore in revenue
  • Paisabazaar's loan disbursals reached Rs 4,366 crore, up 33% year-on-year, with an annualized run rate of Rs 17,500 crore

PB Fintech, the parent company of insurance marketplace Policybazaar and credit platform Paisabazaar, posted a 92% jump in net profit for the April-June quarter of FY27, powered by sharp margin improvements across its core insurance distribution business.

The Gurugram-based company reported a net profit of Rs 163 crore for the quarter, up from Rs 85 crore a year earlier. Operating revenues climbed 40% to Rs 1,888 crore, with total insurance premiums rising 41% year-on-year to Rs 8,372 crore, according to the company's earnings filing.

Margin Expansion Drives the Beat

The standout metric was profitability. EBITDA expanded fourfold to Rs 139 crore, and profit margins improved to 9% from 6% in the year-ago quarter. PB Fintech's post-tax profit exceeded its EBITDA because of Rs 93 crore in non-operating income during the quarter.

The core online insurance distribution business, which remains the company's revenue backbone, generated Rs 1,194 crore. New business verticals — including offline distributor-based insurance, international operations, and corporate sales — contributed Rs 694 crore.

"Q1 is the weakest quarter in the year and Q4 is the biggest. If you are going for efficiency, the first thing you would do is hire nobody in Q1. We hired, at a gross level, 5,000 people in Q1. That explains how much we are trying to reduce costs."

— Yashish Dahiya, Co-founder and Group CEO, PB Fintech

Insurance Premiums Power Growth

Health and life insurance have been the primary growth drivers for Policybazaar as rising financial awareness in India pushes more consumers toward online insurance platforms. The 41% premium growth in Q1 builds on several quarters of strong momentum.

India's insurance penetration remains low compared to developed markets, giving platforms like Policybazaar a long runway. Regulatory changes, including last year's elimination of the 18% GST on life and health insurance, have further boosted retail demand.

The new initiatives vertical, while still lossmaking, showed progress. Its adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 18% to Rs 36 crore, as the core business's profitability gains more than offset the drag.

Paisabazaar Gains Traction

On the lending side, Paisabazaar disbursed Rs 4,366 crore in loans during the quarter, a 33% increase year-on-year. The platform said it is disbursing loans and credit cards at an annualized run rate of Rs 17,500 crore and 370,000, respectively.

The credit business had faced headwinds after the Reserve Bank of India's crackdown on unsecured lending in late 2024. Paisabazaar has since pivoted toward secured credit products, including home loans and loans against property, through its PB Connect offering.

Renewal revenue — a key indicator of customer retention and long-term value — has been growing steadily, reflecting the compounding effect of three years of premium growth.

Market Reaction and Outlook

PB Fintech's stock closed 1.3% higher on the BSE at Rs 1,630 before the results were announced, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 75,419 crore. The results were declared post market hours.

Dahiya signaled that the company is prioritizing growth over cost-cutting in its weakest seasonal quarter, a strategy that bets on renewals catching up as past growth compounds. Investors in the Indian insurtech space — including NRI investors tracking the sector — will watch whether the margin trajectory holds through the stronger second half of the fiscal year.

For diaspora investors tracking India's fintech sector, PB Fintech's results underscore the ongoing profitability inflection in a market where online insurance penetration still has significant room to grow.
